newsitem.title: FRANCE: Elf opens door to Sanofi merger.
newsitem.headline: Elf opens door to Sanofi merger.

text.p: French oil company Elf Aquitaine opened the door on Thursday to a merger between its pharmaceuticals subsidiary, Sanofi, and other drugs laboratories to boost its profitability.
A statement said Elf would not insist on keeping its majority stake in Sanofi but would remain an "important shareholder" in the health and beauty products firm.
Elf has a 55 percent stake in Sanofi before dilution of convertible loans, which would reduce the stake to 53 percent.
"It would be desirable for Sanofi to move nearer other pharmaceutical laboratories, through a merger, in order to speed up its development and increase its profitability," Elf said.
It said the decision to seek a merger was taken at a meeting of its board on Wednesday at which it discussed the group's long term development plans.
Just last month, Elf ruled out a merger for Sanofi, such as an often rumoured link with Rhone-Poulenc drugs unit Rhone-Poulenc Rorer, saying it wanted to let the subsidiary grow through alliances.
Analysts said Rhone-Poulenc's U.S.-quoted subsidiary was still one of the favourite candidates for a Sanofi tie-up.
"Everything is open I guess, but Rhone-Poulenc Rorer would be the most likely the candidate. They would fit," said one drugs industry analyst at a Paris brokerage.
An Elf spokesman said the company had not yet started talks with anyone over a Sanofi merger.
Sanofi said in November it was willing to participate in a prudent way in the restructuring of the pharmaceuticals industry through acquisitions.
The company made a first-half 1996 net profit of 616 million francs, up 11 percent from the same period last year.
A merger for Sanofi would be the latest move in a wave of consolidation of the pharmaceuticals industry worldwide.
Earlier this month, German chemicals giant Hoechst which holds 56.53 percent of French pharmaceuticals group Roussel Uclaf, announced an 18.1 billion franc offer to buy out minority shareholders.

In a separate merger announcement on Thursday, Rhone-Poulenc said it would combine its animal health and poultry engineering activities with those of U.S. drugs company Merck & Co Inc to form the world's largest operator in the sector.
